notes: Which effort levels a model supports depends on the model; Claude Code falls back to the highest supported level at or below the one asked for. ultracode is not a level: it asks for xhigh with ultracode on, under which Claude Code plans a dynamic workflow for each substantive task.

Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium; Opus 4.7 defaults to xhigh; other models that support effort default to high. Anthropic suggests medium for clearly scoped feature work, high where verification matters or edge cases are likely (such as a bug fix in an existing codebase), and max only for hard problems worked through unattended, where it may overthink.
Model aliases: opus, sonnet, haiku, fable (the Fable model, for the hardest and longest-running tasks) and best (the same model as opus).

Opus 5.5 may decline a request that pushes it to reproduce its internal reasoning in the reply (refusal category reasoning_extraction); ask for a short explanation or a summary of what it did instead.
These are the documented model-advertised effort levels; model_reasoning_effort is a string, not a fixed global enum, and the levels available depend on the selected model and client.
For GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, OpenAI recommends starting with the effort the client selects and adjusting it for the task; for GPT-6 Astra, starting at low.
For GPT-6 Luna, OpenAI recommends starting at high; it supports efforts through max, but not ultra.
Max gives a single task more time to reason; ultra uses subagents for separate parts of complex work in parallel. OpenAI says most tasks do not need max or ultra.
